blindSummary: Courts struck down the buggery laws in 2022; this country has an organised LGBT community and a functioning state. No legal gender recognition; modest social conservatism; tourist areas accustomed to diverse visitors.
blindOutOfScope: No legal gender recognition; thin trans-specific data.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust page documents regional constitutional challenges to criminalising laws; this country decriminalised same-sex conduct in December 2022 via such a constitutional challenge.

NOTE: This international human-rights organisation's article is about another state's 2022 ruling, not this country specifically; included as regional context (this country's own high court struck down its buggery and indecency laws the same year).

Advocacy news archive (Nov 2018): first-person account by a trans activist of this country - the country's first vigil of an international transgender day of remembrance; rising trans murder rates globally (369 reported in 2018); her own brush with death; notes 62% of trans murder victims are sex workers and misgendering of victims as 'cross-dressers'.

Advocacy news archive (April 2019): the man who attacked the activist with a meat cleaver (Feb 2018, serious injuries including to her throat) was ordered to pay a fine of about 460 units of local currency or serve three months - effectively no jail time; she led the country's first Pride (2017) and is lead claimant in the challenge to the anti-sodomy law (carrying life imprisonment, described as the harshest law of its kind in this part of the world).

Advocacy news archive commentary (Aug 2020) by the same activist: a 2020 employment anti-discrimination bill omitted gender identity - trans people are frequently denied or fired from jobs for 'dressing wrong'; she herself was terminated by a law firm after legally changing her name; the country's remote-worker visa scheme is tainted by discriminatory laws.

Overseas LGBT news outlet (June 2018): activists here (a trans woman as lead claimant, with international support) filed the first challenge to the country's sexual-offences law at a regional human-rights commission - the law puts trans people in legal jeopardy and enables prejudice and violence.
blindTangential: The 2022 court decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
